# Report conflicts as data and resolve them without a clone

## Intent

When a rebase on the hub cannot be done, an agent gets the reason as data it can act on: which files conflict, what kind of conflict each one is, and which landed changes it collided with. An agent that has no clone can then read a conflicted file with conflict markers and hand its resolution back through the API, so that a conflict never forces anyone to fetch the repository.

## Goals

- One conflict report shape, in one type with one attribution of landed changes, for every place where a rebase can fail on the hub: `target_sha`, `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `commit_sha`, `files`, `landed_changes` and `change`.
- Every conflicted file is reported with one of eight kinds (`content`, `add_add`, `modify_delete`, `delete_modify`, `rename`, `mode`, `binary`, `submodule`) and with its three sides (`base`, `ours`, `theirs`).
- `GET /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/conflict` answers the change's current conflict report, computed against the present head it would be rebased onto.
- `GET /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/conflict/file?path=` answers a `content`-conflicted file as text with the markers `<<<<<<< target`, `=======` and `>>>>>>> change`.
- `POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/restack` accepts `resolutions` and uses them wherever a listed path conflicts during the replay; success records a `restack` version authored by the caller.
- `parley change conflict` and `parley change resolve` drive those routes from the shell.

## Non-goals

- The land attempt, the landing algorithm, the `409 land_conflict` answer and the `parley.change.land_fail` event: package 25 optimistic_landing. It is built before this package and produces the report of a failed land itself, in the `ConflictReport` type of `internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go`, with the attribution of landed changes in `internal/land/conflict.go` and the `change` member of a stack land; this package reuses both and defines no second type.

- The comparison route and its trial rebase, and the server-side rebase route with its `409 rebase_conflict`: packages 20 scm_read_api and 21 scm_write_api. They carry a report of this type, `ConflictReport`, which package 20 declares in `internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go` with `landed_changes` and every `landed_by` empty.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new, except that the restack operation in `internal/change/` and the command file `internal/cli/change.go` are first created by packages 22 to 24 and extended here, and that `internal/gitrepo/` is first created by the packages this one depends on. The source is `docs/prd/08_landing_and_policy.md`: §8.3.3 (the conflict report), LAND-FR-030 to LAND-FR-032, the two `conflict` routes of §8.5, the two CLI entries `parley change conflict` and `parley change resolve` of §8.6, and the part of LAND-FR-003 that names the two routes. The restack route is in `docs/prd/07_changes_and_stacks.md` (CHG-FR-034 and its entry in §7.5). User stories: LAND-US-02 and LAND-US-03.

A rebase on the hub is a replay: the commits of some work that are not in its base are applied one after the other on top of a commit, the *onto* commit. Landing replays onto the target head, a restack onto the head of the change below or onto the target, the server-side rebase and the comparison onto a named ref. When one commit does not apply, the replay stops and nothing is moved.

The code of this package lives in `internal/land/` (the attribution it shares with landing and the two read handlers), `internal/gitrepo/` (the conflict report type and what a failed replay step tells about each conflicted path, both first added by package 20 and completed here, and the marker text), `internal/change/` (resolutions in the restack) and `internal/cli/change.go` (the two commands).

## Requirements

### The conflict report (§8.3.3)

The report is built whenever a replay stops at a commit that does not apply. It has exactly seven members:

| Member | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `target_sha` | string | the commit the work was being replayed onto |
| `head_sha` | string | the head that was being replayed |
| `base_sha` | string | the commit the work was based on before |
| `commit_sha` | string | the first commit of the work that did not apply |
| `files` | object[] | one entry per conflicted path of that commit, ordered by `path` |
| `landed_changes` | object[] | `{number, title, landed_sha, session_id}` for each change that landed between `base_sha` and `target_sha` and touched a conflicted path, ordered by `number`; empty when unknown |
| `change` | int or null | in a stack land, the change that conflicted; null everywhere else |

All commit ids are full 40-character ids. A file entry has `path` (the path in the target), `kind`, `base`, `ours`, `theirs` and `landed_by`. `base`, `ours` and `theirs` are `{sha, mode, path}` of the file in the common ancestor (the parent of `commit_sha`), in the target as replayed so far (`ours`) and in the commit of the change (`theirs`); each is null where the file does not exist on that side. `landed_by` holds the numbers of the landed changes that touched this path, ascending, and is empty when none is known.

The kinds:

| `kind` | When |
|---|---|
| `submodule` | the path is a submodule entry (mode `160000`) on any side |
| `binary` | both sides changed the content of a file that git treats as binary |
| `rename` | one side renamed the file and the other side renamed it to another path, deleted it, or added a file at the new path |
| `add_add` | the file has no common ancestor and both sides added different content at the path; also a path that is a file on one side and a directory on the other |
| `modify_delete` | the target changed the file and the change deleted it |
| `delete_modify` | the target deleted the file and the change changed it |
| `mode` | both sides give the file different modes and the content is the same or merges |
| `content` | both sides changed the text of the file and the changes overlap |

Where several rows apply to one path the first row in this order wins. The report is the same JSON wherever it appears: as the `conflict` member of a change, of a land attempt and of a comparison, and as `details` of the error envelope with `409 rebase_conflict`.

`landed_changes` is known when `base_sha` is an ancestor of `target_sha`: the attribution of `internal/land/conflict.go` (first added by package 25 for landing) then takes the commits between the two, asks the commit mapping of landing which landed change each belongs to, and keeps the changes with a commit that touched a conflicted path. Commits that belong to no change (a direct push, a sync from origin) contribute nothing. When `base_sha` is not an ancestor of `target_sha`, or the mapping cannot be read, `landed_changes` and every `landed_by` are empty and the report is still produced.

Building a report changes nothing: no ref of the repository moves and no working directory is left behind.

### Reading the current report (LAND-FR-030, `GET /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/conflict`)

The route needs `changes:read` (PATs) and read access to the workspace, which is the change's target workspace. It answers `200` with `{"mergeable": "clean" | "conflict", "conflict": <conflict report> | null}`.

The answer is about the present. The *onto* commit of a change is the current head of the change below it when it has a `depends_on`, and the current head of its target branch otherwise. For a `draft` or `open` change, the stored report is used only when the change's `mergeable` is `conflict` and the stored report's `target_sha` and `head_sha` equal the present onto commit and the change's present head. In every other case (the target moved, a new version arrived, `mergeable` is `unknown` or `clean`) the hub runs a trial replay of the change's own commits onto the onto commit and answers from it: `clean` with `conflict: null`, or `conflict` with a fresh report. The read stores nothing and emits no event.

For a `landed` or `abandoned` change nothing is recomputed: the answer is `conflict` with the stored report when the change holds one, and `clean` with `null` otherwise.

Failures: `403 insufficient_scope` for a PAT without `changes:read`; `404 not_found` for a workspace the caller cannot read; `404`, `error_type: change_not_found`, for an unknown number; `409`, `error_type: conflict`, when the target branch of a `draft` or `open` change no longer exists. A token bound to a fork F reaches the route on F's parent only for a change whose source workspace is F; for any other change it gets `404 change_not_found` (LAND-FR-003).

### Reading a conflicted file (LAND-FR-031, `GET …/conflict/file?path=`)

Same scope, access and fork-token rule as the report route. `path` is required; without it, or empty, the answer is `400 invalid_request`. The hub takes the current report as the report route does. When `path` is a `content` entry of it, the answer is `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and the merged file: the text both sides agree on, and each overlapping region written as

```
<<<<<<< target
(lines of the target)
=======
(lines of the change)
>>>>>>> change
```

The sides are those of the report entry: `ours` is the target as replayed so far, `theirs` the file in `commit_sha`.

Failures: `404`, `error_type: path_not_found`, when the path is not in the current report (which includes every path of a change that is `clean`); `409`, `error_type: not_text_conflict`, when the entry has any other kind.

### Restack with resolutions (LAND-FR-032, `POST …/changes/:number/restack`)

The restack body takes an optional `resolutions` list. Each entry has a `path` and exactly one of `content` (a UTF-8 string), `content_base64` (standard base64 of the bytes) or `delete: true`.

During the replay of package 24, at each commit that does not apply, the hub looks at the conflicted paths of that commit. When every one of them is listed, it takes the listed result for each path (the given bytes, or no file for `delete`) in place of the conflict, keeps what merged cleanly everywhere else, and goes on with the next commit. A path that conflicts in several commits gets its resolution in each of them. A listed path that does not conflict is left as the replay produced it. A resolved file keeps the mode it has in the change; when the change has no file there, the mode it has in the target; otherwise `100644`.

When a conflicted path is not listed, the restack fails as it does without resolutions: `409 rebase_conflict` with the conflict report in `details`, no branch moves and no version is recorded.

Success answers `200 {"status": "restacked", "change": <change object>}`. The source branch moves by compare-and-swap, and the new version has kind `restack` and is `created_by` the caller, not `system`; it then goes through policy like any other version. A change that is already built on its onto commit answers `200` with `status: "up_to_date"` and the resolutions are not used.

Validation, before anything is replayed, each `400 invalid_request`: `resolutions` is not a list; an entry has no `path`, an empty one, one that starts with `/`, or one with an empty, `.` or `..` segment; an entry has none or more than one of `content`, `content_base64` and `delete`; `delete` is `false`; `content_base64` is not valid base64; two entries name the same path.

### `parley change conflict <slug> <number>` (§8.6)

Calls `GET …/changes/:number/conflict`, prints the response body and exits 0. With `--fail-on-conflict`, a response with `mergeable: "conflict"` is still printed on stdout, `condition_not_met` is reported on stderr and the exit status is 3.

With `--file <path>` it calls `GET …/changes/:number/conflict/file` with the path as the query parameter and writes the response text to stdout byte for byte, not wrapped in JSON. `--file` together with `--fail-on-conflict` is a usage error (exit status 2, no request). A hub error is printed as the envelope on stderr and exits 1.

### `parley change resolve <slug> <number>` (§8.6)

Flags: `--file <repo-path>=<local-file>` (repeatable) and `--delete <repo-path>` (repeatable). The command reads each local file and calls `POST …/changes/:number/restack` with one resolution per flag: `{path, content_base64}` for `--file`, `{path, delete: true}` for `--delete`. It prints the response body and exits 0. A `409 rebase_conflict` is printed as the envelope, with the report, on stderr, and exits 1.

Usage errors, each with exit status 2 and no request: neither flag given; a `--file` value without `=`, or with an empty repository path or an empty local path; a local file that cannot be read; the same repository path named twice across both flags.

### End-to-end flow

An agent's change stops applying because another change landed on the same lines. The agent runs `parley change conflict demo 2` and reads the report; `parleyd` runs the trial replay and names the file as `content` and the landed change as `landed_by`. The agent runs `parley change conflict demo 2 --file app.txt` and gets the file with markers, writes the resolved file locally, and runs `parley change resolve demo 2 --file app.txt=./app.txt`. `parleyd` replays the change with the resolution, moves the source branch and records a `restack` version authored by the agent. `parley change conflict demo 2` now reports `clean`.

## Design Decisions

1. One type, one classification, one attribution. The conflict report type is `ConflictReport` of `internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go` and the classification of a conflicted path is that of the trial rebase beside it, both declared by the earliest producer (package 20) and used by packages 21, 23, 24 and 25; this package completes them there (the kind order, the file-against-directory case, the ordering of `files`) and declares no second type. The attribution that fills `landed_changes` and `landed_by` is the function package 25 adds in `internal/land/conflict.go`; it reads landed changes through a small lookup. `internal/change/` and `internal/scm/` cannot import `internal/land/`, so each takes the attribution as a function value that `parleyd` hands it, and the producers built before this package (comparison, server-side rebase, mergeability, restack) are switched to call it. The PRD names one shape for all of them and no owner.
2. `ours` is the target and `theirs` is the change, so `modify_delete` means "the target changed it, the change deleted it" and `delete_modify` the reverse. The PRD lists both kinds without saying which side is which; this follows the `base`/`ours`/`theirs` order of §8.3.3.
3. One path gets one kind; the order submodule, binary, rename, add_add, modify_delete or delete_modify, mode, content decides. The PRD gives no precedence; the order goes from what a text resolution can least express to what it can.
4. A file on one side against a directory on the other is reported as `add_add`. The PRD's enum has no kind for it and it is the nearest: both sides put something at the path.
5. `files` is ordered by path and `landed_changes` by number, so that two reports of the same conflict are byte-identical.
6. The report read uses the stored report only when it matches the present pair of commits and recomputes otherwise; it stores nothing and emits nothing. The PRD says "recomputed when stale"; a `GET` without side effects leaves package 23 the only writer of `mergeable`.
7. For a dependent change the onto commit is the head of the change below, as in §7.3.4, not the target head.
8. A `landed` or `abandoned` change answers from what is stored, without recomputing. The PRD names no error for it and there is nothing left to rebase.
9. A `draft` or `open` change whose target branch is gone answers `409`, `error_type: conflict`. Its `mergeable` is `unknown` (§7.10) and the response allows only `clean` or `conflict`; the generic type of PLAT-FR-012 is used because §8 defines no specific one.
10. A missing or empty `path` on the file route is `400 invalid_request`. The PRD marks it required and names no error.
11. A listed resolution is used only where its path conflicts, and at every commit where it does. This is the plain reading of "wherever a listed path conflicts".
12. Resolutions are validated as a whole before the replay, and a duplicate path is refused. The PRD gives the entry shape and no errors; refusing early means a bad list never moves a branch.
13. A resolved file takes its mode from the change, then the target, then `100644`. Resolutions carry no mode in the PRD.
14. `parley change conflict --file` prints the file as raw text. PLAT-FR-092 says stdout carries one JSON document, and §8.6 says the flag prints "that file with conflict markers"; the file itself is what an agent saves and edits.
15. `--file` with `--fail-on-conflict` is a usage error: the file route has no `mergeable` to test.
16. `parley change resolve` always sends `content_base64`, so that any file, text or binary, travels unchanged. A `--file` value is split at its first `=`.
17. Language Go; the server runs the `git` command (2.38 or later) as a subprocess through `internal/gitrepo`, and no git library; tests create repositories with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`; HTTP is `net/http`, the CLI is `github.com/spf13/cobra` (project-wide decisions 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7).

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Version**: One head of a change's source branch. Every push, API commit or restack that moves the source creates a new version. Old versions stay fetchable.
- **Stack**: Changes linked by `depends_on`, lowest first.
- **Restack**: The hub rebasing a dependent change onto the new head of the change below it, or onto the target once that change has landed.
- **Landing**: Adding a change's commits to its target branch: a server-side rebase followed by a compare-and-swap of the target ref.
- **Land attempt**: One request to land a change (or a stack), with its outcome.
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent.
- **Replay**: In this package, applying the commits of some work that are not in its base, one after the other, on top of an onto commit.
- **Onto commit**: The commit a replay builds on: the target head, or for a dependent change the head of the change below.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: One conflict report for every failed replay

**Rationale:** An agent can only fix a conflict it can read as data, and it should not have to learn a different shape for landing, restack, rebase and comparison.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a replay of the commits of some work onto an onto commit stops at a commit that does not apply, THE parleyd SHALL build a conflict report whose target_sha is the onto commit, head_sha the head that was replayed, base_sha the commit the work was based on before, commit_sha the first commit that did not apply, files one entry per conflicted path of that commit ordered by path, and change null, with every commit id written as its full 40-character id
   → a JSON object with exactly the seven members {target_sha, head_sha, base_sha, commit_sha, files: [{path, kind, base, ours, theirs, landed_by}], landed_changes: [{number, title, landed_sha, session_id}], change}; every sha is 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters; change is null
   Check: integration
   - setup: a repository made with git init in a temporary directory
   - setup: the real git command
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_test.go: repo with main at B; work = three commits W1, W2, W3 on B where W2 edits line 1 of a.txt and b.txt; target = one commit T on B that edits line 1 of a.txt and b.txt differently; rep = BuildReport(repo, onto=T, head=W3, base=B); assert rep.target_sha == T; assert rep.head_sha == W3; assert rep.base_sha == B; assert rep.commit_sha == W2; assert paths(rep.files) == ['a.txt', 'b.txt']; assert rep.change == null; assert keys(json(rep)) == the seven members; assert every sha matches ^[0-9a-f]{40}$; a second case where the work applies: assert the replay reports no conflict and no report is built
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any conflicted path, report exactly one kind, the first that applies in this order: submodule (mode 160000 on any side), binary (both sides changed a file git treats as binary), rename (one side renamed the file and the other renamed it elsewhere, deleted it or added a file at the new path), add_add (no common ancestor and different content on both sides, or a file on one side and a directory on the other), modify_delete (the target changed it, the change deleted it), delete_modify (the target deleted it, the change changed it), mode (different modes and content that merges), content (overlapping text changes)
   → files[].kind is one of content, add_add, modify_delete, delete_modify, rename, mode, binary, submodule
   Check: integration
   - setup: repositories made with git init in temporary directories
   - setup: the real git command
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_test.go, a table of nine repositories, each with one conflicting commit, and the kind expected for its path: {both edit line 1 of a text file -> content; both add f.txt with different text -> add_add; target edits f.txt, change deletes it -> modify_delete; target deletes f.txt, change edits it -> delete_modify; target renames f.txt to g.txt, change renames it to h.txt -> rename; both add f.sh with the same content, the target with mode 100755 and the change with mode 100644 -> mode; both replace a file holding NUL bytes with different bytes -> binary; both move a 160000 entry to different commits -> submodule; target adds file d, change adds file d/x -> add_add}: rep = BuildReport(...); assert kind of the path == expected; assert each path appears once
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any conflicted path, report base, ours and theirs as {sha, mode, path} of the file in the parent of commit_sha, in the target as replayed so far, and in commit_sha, and report null for a side on which the file does not exist
   → files[].base, files[].ours, files[].theirs: {sha: 40 hexadecimal characters, mode: string such as 100644, path: string} or null
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_test.go, over the same repositories as the kind table: content case: assert base.sha, ours.sha and theirs.sha equal git rev-parse of B:a.txt, T:a.txt and W:a.txt and all modes == '100644'; add_add case: assert base == null and ours != null and theirs != null; modify_delete case: assert theirs == null and ours.sha == rev-parse(T:f.txt); delete_modify case: assert ours == null; rename case: assert ours.path == 'g.txt' and theirs.path == 'h.txt' and base.path == 'f.txt'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHILE base_sha is an ancestor of target_sha, THE parleyd SHALL list in landed_changes, ordered by number, every landed change that has a commit between base_sha and target_sha touching a conflicted path, each as {number, title, landed_sha, session_id}, and list in each file entry's landed_by the numbers, ascending, of the landed changes that touched that path, counting no commit that belongs to no change
   → landed_changes: [{number: int, title: string, landed_sha: 40 hexadecimal characters, session_id: string or null}]; files[].landed_by: int[]
   Check: integration
   - setup: a landed-change lookup backed by a table of commit id to change, standing in for the commit mapping of package 25
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_test.go: target history after B: commit L1 mapped to landed change 7 (title 'seven', session s-1) edits a.txt; commit L2 mapped to landed change 8 edits other.txt; commit D mapped to no change (a direct push) edits b.txt; work edits a.txt and b.txt on B; rep = BuildReport(repo, onto=target, head, base=B, lookup); assert rep.landed_changes == [{number: 7, title: 'seven', landed_sha: L1, session_id: 's-1'}]; assert landed_by('a.txt') == [7]; assert landed_by('b.txt') == []
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF base_sha is not an ancestor of target_sha, or the landed-change lookup returns an error, THEN THE parleyd SHALL produce the report with landed_changes empty and every landed_by empty
   → the report is returned without error; landed_changes == [] and every files[].landed_by == []; neither member is null
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_test.go, a table over {base on a branch unrelated to the target, a lookup that returns an error}: rep, err = BuildReport(...); assert err == nil; assert json(rep).landed_changes == []; assert every json(rep).files[i].landed_by == []; assert len(rep.files) > 0
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any replay it runs to build a report or a trial result, leave every ref of the repository at the commit it had before and leave no working directory or temporary index behind, whether the replay conflicts, applies or fails
   → git for-each-ref prints the same lines before and after; the temporary directory of the hub holds no entry created by the call
   Check: property
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_test.go, over the nine repositories of the kind table plus one clean replay and one replay with an unknown head sha: before = git for-each-ref; files = list(scratch dir); BuildReport or TrialReplay(...); assert git for-each-ref == before; assert list(scratch dir) == files
   ```

### REQ-2: Read a change's current conflict report

**Rationale:** An agent that is told its change conflicts needs the report as it is now, not as it was when the last background check ran.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a caller with changes:read and read access requests GET /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/conflict for a draft or open change whose mergeable is conflict and whose stored report has target_sha equal to the present onto commit and head_sha equal to the change's present head, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the stored report without running a replay, where the onto commit is the head of the change below for a change with depends_on and the head of the target branch otherwise

### REQ-3: Read a conflicted file with markers

**Rationale:** An agent without a clone has no other way to see both sides of a conflict in the form every tool and model already understands.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a caller with changes:read and read access requests GET /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/conflict/file with a path that is a content entry of the change's current report, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the merged text of the file in which each overlapping region is written as a line <<<<<<< target, the lines of the target as replayed so far, a line =======, the lines of the file in commit_sha, and a line >>>>>>> change, and every other line appears once
   → HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/plain; charset=utf-8 and the marked text as the body
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub with a real repository made with git init and open change 2 that conflicts in app.txt
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_handlers_test.go: base app.txt = 'one\ntwo\nthree\n'; target changes line 2 to 'TARGET'; the change changes line 2 to 'CHANGE' and appends 'four'; r = GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/2/conflict/file?path=app.txt; assert r.status == 200; assert r.header['Content-Type'] == 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'; assert r.body == 'one\n<<<<<<< target\nTARGET\n=======\nCHANGE\n>>>>>>> change\nthree\nfour\n'; a second case with path 'dir/a b.txt' sent percent-encoded: assert status 200
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any request to GET …/conflict/file, take the current report by the rule of GET …/conflict: the stored report when it matches the present onto commit and head, a trial replay otherwise
   → the body reflects the present target head, not the head the stored report was computed for
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_handlers_test.go: stored report says app.txt conflicts with target line 'TARGET'; add a commit to the target that sets the line to 'TARGET2'; r = GET .../conflict/file?path=app.txt; assert r.status == 200; assert r.body contains 'TARGET2\n=======' and does not contain 'TARGET\n======='
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF GET …/conflict/file is requested without a path parameter or with an empty one, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_handlers_test.go, a table over the queries {'', '?path='}: r = GET .../conflict/file + query; assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF the path given to GET …/conflict/file is not an entry of the change's current report, which includes every path of a change that is clean, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 404 with error_type path_not_found
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_handlers_test.go, a table over {a conflicting change and a path it changed without conflict, a conflicting change and a path that exists nowhere, a clean change and a path it changed}: r = GET .../conflict/file?path=p; assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'path_not_found'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] IF the path given to GET …/conflict/file is an entry of the current report whose kind is not content, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 409 with error_type not_text_conflict
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/land/conflict_handlers_test.go, a table over changes whose only conflict has kind {add_add, modify_delete, delete_modify, rename, mode, binary, submodule}: r = GET .../conflict/file?path=<entry path>; assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'not_text_conflict'
   ```

### REQ-4: Restack with resolutions

**Rationale:** Reading a conflict is only half of working without a clone; the agent must also be able to hand the fixed file back and get a version that applies.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a caller who may restack the change sends POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/restack with resolutions that list every path that conflicts during the replay, THE parleyd SHALL replay the change's own commits onto the onto commit, taking at each commit that does not apply the listed bytes for a path given with content or content_base64 and no file for a path given with delete: true, move the source branch to the result by compare-and-swap, and record a new version of kind restack whose created_by is the caller
   → HTTP 200 with body {status: "restacked", change: <change object>}; change.version is one higher than before; the new version has kind restack and created_by.actor_id equal to the caller's id; the file at the listed path in change.head_sha has exactly the given bytes, or does not exist for delete
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub with real repositories made with git init, the restack route of package 24 and open change 2 authored by agent A
   ```
   in internal/change/resolutions_test.go, a table over {content: 'one\nMERGED\nthree\n' for a content conflict in app.txt; content_base64 of bytes 00 01 02 for a binary conflict in logo.bin; delete: true for a modify_delete conflict in old.txt}: v0 = change.version; r = POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/2/restack {resolutions: [entry]} as agent A; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.status == 'restacked'; assert r.json.change.version == v0 + 1; ver = GET .../versions/<v0+1>; assert ver.kind == 'restack'; assert ver.created_by.actor_id == A.id and ver.created_by.actor_type != 'system'; assert git rev-parse refs/heads/<source branch> == r.json.change.head_sha; assert git cat-file blob <head>:<path> == given bytes, or for delete that git cat-file -e <head>:old.txt fails; assert git merge-base --is-ancestor <target head> <head>
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any path that conflicts in more than one commit of one replay, use the path's resolution at each of those commits, and give a resolved file the mode it has in the change, else the mode it has in the target, else 100644
   → the restack answers HTTP 200 with status restacked; the path has the given bytes in every replayed commit from the first conflicting one on; its mode in change.head_sha equals its mode in the version that was restacked
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/change/resolutions_test.go: the change has two commits that each edit line 1 of run.sh (mode 100755); the target edits line 1 too; r = POST .../restack {resolutions: [{path: 'run.sh', content: 'final\n'}]}; assert r.status == 200; for each of the two new commits c: assert git cat-file blob c:run.sh == 'final\n'; assert mode of run.sh in git ls-tree <head> == '100755'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHILE a path listed in resolutions does not conflict at a commit of the replay, or the change is already built on its onto commit, THE parleyd SHALL leave that path as the replay produced it and ignore its resolution
   → HTTP 200; the content of the non-conflicting listed path in change.head_sha is the replay's own result, not the listed bytes; an already current change answers {status: "up_to_date"} with change.version unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/change/resolutions_test.go: case 1: the change edits app.txt (conflicts) and adds notes.txt = 'mine\n' (no conflict); r = POST .../restack {resolutions: [{path: 'app.txt', content: ok}, {path: 'notes.txt', content: 'IGNORED\n'}, {path: 'ghost.txt', delete: true}]}; assert r.status == 200; assert blob <head>:notes.txt == 'mine\n'; case 2: a change already on the target head: r = POST .../restack {resolutions: [{path: 'app.txt', content: 'x'}]}; assert r.json.status == 'up_to_date'; assert r.json.change.version unchanged; assert the source branch did not move
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] IF a commit of the replay conflicts on at least one path that resolutions does not list, THEN THE parleyd SHALL fail the restack, move no branch and record no version
   → HTTP 409 with error_type rebase_conflict and the conflict report as error.details, whose files include the unlisted path; the source branch, change.version and change.head_sha are as before
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/change/resolutions_test.go: the change conflicts in a.txt and b.txt; head0 = rev-parse source branch; v0 = change.version; r = POST .../restack {resolutions: [{path: 'a.txt', content: 'x\n'}]}; assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'rebase_conflict'; assert 'b.txt' in paths(r.json.error.details.files); assert r.json.error.details.commit_sha matches ^[0-9a-f]{40}$; assert rev-parse source branch == head0; assert GET change .version == v0
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] IF the resolutions member of a restack body is not a list, or an entry has a missing or empty path, a path that starts with / or has an empty, . or .. segment, none or more than one of content, content_base64 and delete, delete set to false, a content_base64 that is not valid standard base64, or a path that another entry also names, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before any replay, move no branch and record no version
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; the source branch and change.version are as before
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/change/resolutions_test.go, a table over the bodies {resolutions: 'x'; [{content: 'a'}]; [{path: '', content: 'a'}]; [{path: '/a.txt', content: 'a'}]; [{path: 'a/../b', content: 'a'}]; [{path: 'a//b', content: 'a'}]; [{path: './a', content: 'a'}]; [{path: 'a.txt'}]; [{path: 'a.txt', content: 'a', delete: true}]; [{path: 'a.txt', content: 'a', content_base64: 'YQ=='}]; [{path: 'a.txt', delete: false}]; [{path: 'a.txt', content_base64: '***'}]; [{path: 'a.txt', content: 'a'}, {path: 'a.txt', delete: true}]} against a change that conflicts in a.txt: r = POST .../restack body; assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert the source branch and change.version are unchanged; and one accepted body [{path: 'a.txt', content: ''}] (an empty file): assert r.status == 200
   ```
1. [REQ-4.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any restack that succeeds with resolutions, pass the new version through the version recording that every version passes, so that the change's landing is evaluated again for the new head and its mergeable is no longer conflict
   → the change read after the restack has landing.status computed for the new head_sha, needs_restack false, and GET …/conflict answers {mergeable: "clean", conflict: null}
   Check: same as PATH-1

### REQ-5: parley change conflict

**Rationale:** Agents and scripts ask for the report and the marked file from the shell and branch on the exit status.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN a user runs parley change conflict <slug> <number> without --file, THE parley CLI SHALL send GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/changes/<number>/conflict and print the response body
   → exit status 0; stdout is the JSON document {mergeable, conflict}; stderr is empty
   Check: unit
   - setup: an httptest hub that records method, raw path and query and returns a canned answer

1. [REQ-5.2] WHERE --fail-on-conflict is given and the hub answers mergeable conflict, THE parley CLI SHALL print the response body on stdout and report the unmet condition
   → exit status 3; stdout is the JSON document with the report; stderr is the error envelope with code 0 and error_type condition_not_met; with a clean answer the exit status is 0 and stderr is empty
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/change_test.go: hub answers conflict: out = run('change', 'conflict', 'demo', '2', '--fail-on-conflict'); assert out.exit == 3; assert json(out.stdout).mergeable == 'conflict'; assert json(out.stderr).error.error_type == 'condition_not_met' and .error.code == 0; hub answers clean: assert out.exit == 0 and out.stderr == ''
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHERE --file <path> is given, THE parley CLI SHALL send GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/changes/<number>/conflict/file with the path as the percent-encoded query parameter path and write the response body to stdout byte for byte, not wrapped in JSON
   → exit status 0; stdout equals the text the hub returned, including its final newline or the lack of one

   ```
   in internal/cli/change_test.go: hub answers 200 text/plain with body 'a\n<<<<<<< target\nb\n=======\nc\n>>>>>>> change'; out = run('change', 'conflict', 'demo', '2', '--file', 'dir/a b&c.txt'); assert recorded path == '/api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/2/conflict/file'; assert the decoded query parameter path == 'dir/a b&c.txt' and the query has no other parameter; assert out.exit == 0; assert out.stdout == hub body exactly
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] IF parley change conflict is run with --file and --fail-on-conflict together, with an argument count other than two, or the hub answers an error, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL fail without printing a result on stdout, and for the two usage cases without sending a request
   → exit status 2 with error_type usage_error and code 0 on stderr and no request for the usage cases; exit status 1 with the hub's error envelope on stderr, as received, for a hub error; stdout is empty in all three
   Check: unit


### REQ-6: parley change resolve

**Rationale:** The resolved file is on the agent's disk; one command has to carry it to the hub and say whether the change now applies.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN a user runs parley change resolve <slug> <number> with at least one --file <repo-path>=<local-file> or --delete <repo-path>, THE parley CLI SHALL read each local file and send POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/changes/<number>/restack with a resolutions list holding {path, content_base64} for each --file, with the value split at its first =, and {path, delete: true} for each --delete, then print the response body
   → exit status 0; stdout is the JSON document {status, change}; the request body has one resolutions entry per flag and no content member
   Check: unit
   - setup: an httptest hub that records the request body and answers 200 {status: 'restacked', change: {...}}
   - setup: local files in a temporary directory
   ```
   in internal/cli/change_test.go: in a temporary directory write m.txt = 'merged\n' and a file named 'v=1.bin' holding the bytes ff 00; out = run('change', 'resolve', 'demo', '2', '--file', 'app.txt=' + dir + '/m.txt', '--file', 'logo.bin=' + dir + '/v=1.bin', '--delete', 'old.txt'); assert the recorded request is POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/2/restack; body = recorded JSON; assert body.resolutions holds exactly {path: 'app.txt', content_base64: 'bWVyZ2VkCg=='}, {path: 'logo.bin', content_base64: '/wA='} and {path: 'old.txt', delete: true}; assert no entry has a content member; assert out.exit == 0; assert json(out.stdout) == hub body
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] IF the hub answers the restack of parley change resolve with HTTP 409 and error_type rebase_conflict, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL print the envelope with its conflict report and fail
   → exit status 1; stderr is the hub's error envelope as received, with error.details holding the report; stdout is empty
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/change_test.go: hub answers 409 {error: {code: 409, error_type: 'rebase_conflict', message: m, details: report}}; out = run('change', 'resolve', 'demo', '2', '--file', 'a.txt=' + local); assert out.exit == 1; assert json(out.stderr).error.details == report; assert out.stdout == ''
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] IF parley change resolve is run with neither --file nor --delete, with a --file value that has no =, an empty repository path or an empty local path, with a local file that cannot be read, with the same repository path named twice across --file and --delete, or with an argument count other than two, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL fail before sending any request
   → exit status 2; stderr is the error envelope with code 0 and error_type usage_error; stdout is empty; the hub receives no request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/change_test.go, a table over the argument lists {['demo', '2']; ['demo', '2', '--file', 'a.txt']; ['demo', '2', '--file', '=x']; ['demo', '2', '--file', 'a.txt=']; ['demo', '2', '--file', 'a.txt=/no/such/file']; ['demo', '2', '--file', 'a.txt=' + local, '--delete', 'a.txt']; ['demo', '2', '--delete', 'a.txt', '--delete', 'a.txt']; ['demo', '--delete', 'a.txt']}: out = run('change', 'resolve', ...args); assert out.exit == 2; assert json(out.stderr).error.error_type == 'usage_error' and .error.code == 0; assert out.stdout == ''; assert the hub's request count == 0
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent without a clone reads a conflict and resolves it

1. **agent** runs parley change conflict demo 2 --fail-on-conflict after another change landed on the same lines of app.txt
2. **parley CLI** sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/2/conflict
3. **parleyd** runs a trial replay of change 2 onto the present head of main, builds the conflict report naming app.txt as content and the landed change in landed_by, and answers 200
4. **parley CLI** prints the report on stdout and exits 3
5. **agent** runs parley change conflict demo 2 --file app.txt and saves the output
6. **parleyd** answers the file as text/plain with the markers <<<<<<< target, ======= and >>>>>>> change
7. **agent** writes the resolved app.txt locally and runs parley change resolve demo 2 --file app.txt=./app.txt
8. **parley CLI** reads the local file and sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/2/restack with one resolution
9. **parleyd** replays change 2 onto the head of main with the resolution, moves the source branch by compare-and-swap, records a restack version authored by the agent, evaluates policy for it and answers 200 with status restacked
10. **agent** runs parley change conflict demo 2 --fail-on-conflict again and gets mergeable clean with exit status 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parley CLI command tree, parleyd HTTP server with its middleware, access component, change store on SQLite, restack operation, conflict report component, the git command on a bare repository on disk

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with an empty data directory
- workspace demo created from a local repository made with git init whose main holds app.txt = 'one\ntwo\nthree\n'
- change 1 (line 2 becomes 'TARGET') and change 2 (line 2 becomes 'CHANGE'), both opened by pushes of an agent's token; change 1 is landed

**End state:**

- the first parley change conflict exits 3 and its report has one file, app.txt, kind content, landed_by [1], and landed_changes with number 1
- the --file output is 'one\n<<<<<<< target\nTARGET\n=======\nCHANGE\n>>>>>>> change\nthree\n'
- parley change resolve exits 0 with status restacked; change 2 has one more version, of kind restack, created_by the agent's user
- the source branch of change 2 points at a commit whose parent is the head of main and whose app.txt is the resolved text
- the last parley change conflict exits 0 and prints mergeable clean with conflict null
- the head of main did not move after change 1 landed

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/conflict_resolution_test.go: hub = startHub(t); create demo; push and open changes 1 and 2; land change 1; c = runCLI('change', 'conflict', 'demo', '2', '--fail-on-conflict'); assert c.exit == 3; rep = json(c.stdout).conflict; assert paths(rep.files) == ['app.txt'] and rep.files[0].kind == 'content' and rep.files[0].landed_by == [1]; f = runCLI('change', 'conflict', 'demo', '2', '--file', 'app.txt'); assert f.stdout == expected marked text; write 'one\nBOTH\nthree\n' to local app.txt; main0 = rev-parse main; r = runCLI('change', 'resolve', 'demo', '2', '--file', 'app.txt=' + local); assert r.exit == 0 and json(r.stdout).status == 'restacked'; head = json(r.stdout).change.head_sha; assert git rev-parse head^ == main0; assert git cat-file blob head:app.txt == 'one\nBOTH\nthree\n'; v = last of GET .../changes/2/versions; assert v.kind == 'restack' and v.created_by.username == agent user; c2 = runCLI('change', 'conflict', 'demo', '2', '--fail-on-conflict'); assert c2.exit == 0 and json(c2.stdout) == {mergeable: 'clean', conflict: null}; assert rev-parse main == main0
```

## Dependencies

- `09` — builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
- `24` — extends the restack operation and its route with resolutions, and through it uses changes, versions, the replay, the access rule, the HTTP conventions and the CLI foundation
- `25` — reuses the attribution of landed changes in internal/land/conflict.go and the commit mapping from landed commits to changes it reads, and serves its read routes beside the land routes

## Tasks

### 1. Build the conflict report from a failed replay step (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.1, REQ-1.2, REQ-1.3, REQ-1.6

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the report behaviours to internal/land/conflict_test.go and internal/gitrepo/conflict_test.go, each on repositories made with git init in t.TempDir(), and confirm they fail
- 1.2 In internal/gitrepo, complete what the replay of packages 20, 21 and 25 already returns for a step that does not apply, so that it describes every conflicted path: the blob id, mode and path of the file in the parent of the commit, in the tree replayed so far and in the commit, each absent where the file does not exist, plus what git said about the path (content, add/add, modify/delete, rename, distinct modes, binary, submodule, file/directory). git merge-tree --write-tree (git 2.38) reports all of this without a working directory; extend the existing replay and add no second one
- 1.3 Use ConflictReport, the type package 20 declares in internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go, with its seven members and the six members of a file entry, and declare no second type; make its encoding write every member (null or an empty list, never left out) and full 40-character commit ids where it does not yet
- 1.4 Complete the build function beside the type: it takes the repository, the onto commit, the head and the base, runs or receives the replay, and on the first commit that does not apply returns the report with files ordered by path and change null; a replay that applies returns no report; internal/land/conflict.go of package 25 keeps only the attribution and the change member of a stack land
- 1.5 Classify each path into exactly one kind by the fixed order submodule, binary, rename, add_add, modify_delete, delete_modify, mode, content; the target is ours and the change is theirs; a file against a directory is add_add
- 1.6 Run every replay without touching a ref and remove any temporary directory or index on every exit, including an error from git
- 1.7 Make every producer built before this package return that one type through that one build function: comparison (package 20), server-side rebase (21), mergeability (23), restack (24) and landing (25); internal/change and internal/scm receive the attribution of task 2 as a function value from parleyd because they cannot import internal/land; landing keeps setting the change member in a stack land

**Touches:**

- `internal/gitrepo/conflict.go`
- `internal/gitrepo/conflict_test.go`
- `internal/gitrepo/conflictreport.go`
- `internal/land/conflict.go`
- `internal/land/conflict_test.go`
- `internal/change/`
- `internal/scm/`
- `cmd/parleyd/`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 2. Name the landed changes a conflict collided with (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.4, REQ-1.5

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the landed-change behaviours to internal/land/conflict_test.go with a lookup backed by a table, and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Reuse the attribution function package 25 adds in internal/land/conflict.go, which fills landed_changes and landed_by through a lookup from a commit id to the landed change it belongs to ({number, title, landed_sha, session_id}); the production lookup reads the commit mapping of package 25; add no second attribution, and extend that function where a behaviour of this task is missing
- 2.3 When base_sha is an ancestor of target_sha, list the commits between them with the paths each touched, keep those touching a conflicted path, and resolve each through the lookup; a commit with no change contributes nothing
- 2.4 Fill landed_changes ordered by number without duplicates, and each entry's landed_by with the ascending numbers for that path
- 2.5 When base_sha is not an ancestor of target_sha, or the lookup returns an error, return the report with landed_changes and every landed_by as empty lists and no error

**Touches:**

- `internal/land/conflict.go`
- `internal/land/conflict_test.go`

### 3. Serve GET …/changes/:number/conflict (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the route's behaviours to internal/land/conflict_handlers_test.go with net/http/httptest and confirm they fail
- 3.2 Register GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/conflict with the server of package 02, needing the scope changes:read and read access to the workspace through the access component of package 07
- 3.3 Look the change up by number in the workspace; answer 404 change_not_found for an unknown number, and for a caller whose token is bound to a fork when the change's source workspace is not that fork (ask the binding component of package 08 what the token covers)
- 3.4 Add one function that returns the current result of a change, used by this route and by the file route: for a landed or abandoned change the stored report or none; for a draft or open change the stored report when mergeable is conflict and its target_sha and head_sha equal the present onto commit and the change's head; otherwise a trial replay of the change's own commits onto the onto commit
- 3.5 Take as onto commit the head of the change below for a change with depends_on, and the head of the target branch otherwise; when the target branch of a draft or open change does not exist, answer 409 with error_type conflict
- 3.6 Answer 200 with {mergeable, conflict}, conflict being null when clean; write nothing to the change and emit no event

**Touches:**

- `internal/land/conflict_handlers.go`
- `internal/land/conflict_handlers_test.go`
- `internal/land/current_conflict.go`

### 5. Accept resolutions in the restack (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4

**Depends on:** 2

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the resolution behaviours to internal/change/resolutions_test.go against the restack route of package 24 on real repositories, and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Parse and validate the resolutions member of the restack body before any replay: a list; each entry a path that is not empty, does not start with / and has no empty, . or .. segment; exactly one of content, content_base64 and delete: true; valid standard base64; no path twice. Any violation answers 400 invalid_request
- 5.3 Extend the replay used by the restack in internal/gitrepo with a resolver: at a commit that does not apply, when every conflicted path has a resolution, build that commit's tree from the cleanly merged result with each conflicted path replaced by the given bytes (or removed for delete), and continue with the next commit; the same resolution is used at every commit where its path conflicts
- 5.4 Give a resolved file the mode it has in the change's commit, else in the tree replayed so far, else 100644
- 5.5 Ignore a resolution whose path does not conflict at a commit, and all of them when the change is already built on its onto commit (status up_to_date)
- 5.6 When a conflicted path has no resolution, stop as the restack of package 24 does: 409 rebase_conflict with the conflict report of this package in details, no branch moved, no version recorded
- 5.7 On success move the source branch by compare-and-swap and record the restack version as the manual restack of package 24 does, through the version recording of package 22 with created_by the caller, so that policy and mergeability are evaluated for it as for any version; answer 200 with status restacked and the change

**Touches:**

- `internal/change/resolutions.go`
- `internal/change/resolutions_test.go`
- `internal/change/`
- `internal/gitrepo/conflict.go`
- `internal/gitrepo/conflict_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 7. Add parley change resolve (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6

**Depends on:** 5, 6

**Steps:**

- 7.1 Add the command's behaviours to internal/cli/change_test.go against an httptest hub that records the request body, and confirm they fail
- 7.2 Add resolve under the change command group of internal/cli/change.go, with exactly two arguments and the repeatable flags --file <repo-path>=<local-file> and --delete <repo-path>
- 7.3 Split each --file value at its first =; fail as a usage error, before any request, when no flag is given, a value has no =, either side is empty, a local file cannot be read, or a repository path occurs twice across both flags
- 7.4 Send POST to the restack route with resolutions holding {path, content_base64} for each --file (the file's bytes in standard base64) and {path, delete: true} for each --delete; print the response body and exit 0
- 7.5 Leave a hub error to the helpers of package 09: the envelope, with the conflict report of a 409 rebase_conflict in details, goes to stderr and the exit status is 1
- 7.6 Add test/e2e/conflict_resolution_test.go with the end-to-end flow of the PRD: start the hub in-process on a loopback port the system picks, make two changes that edit the same line, land the first, and drive conflict, conflict --file and resolve through the CLI command tree

**Touches:**

- `internal/cli/change.go`
- `internal/cli/change_test.go`
- `test/e2e/conflict_resolution_test.go`

**Done when:**
